stories.title: Congress wants probe into conflicting versions in Kishtwar incident : Karra
stories.summary: Jammu, Nov 17: Jammu and Kashmir Pradesh Congress Committee (JKPCC) president Tariq Hameed Karra on Tuesday reiterated that his party wanted probe into conflicting versions vis-a-vis two SPOs' killings in Kishtwar. “Congress objects to the way the BJP has questioned the integrity of Jammu and Kashmir Police (JKP) and used inappropriate words against it. They termed JKP as inefficient and good for nothing which brought down the morale of the entire force (JKP). Secondly, we object to the statements (of BJP leaders) referring to Masjid (mosque). We perceive these statements as attempts aimed at vitiating the atmosphere ahead of Punjab elections,” Karra alleged, while responding to media queries on the sidelines of a party function in Jammu. “You (media) need to ask them (BJP) leaders under what circumstances they made such statements which not only vitiated the atmosphere there (in Kishtwar) but would leave its impact across J&K,” he maintained. Responding to his (Karra's) statement that “SPOs had gone for hunting and were killed in the firing by Army probably due to mistaken identity”, JKPCC president denied having made any statement against the Army. “We did not raise any question about the Army. But what about the charges, they (BJP) have levelled against the Police. We only said that two versions emanated from there (Kishtwar) - one related to militants' angle and the second one related to the Army. We did not level any allegations. We simply said that it was the matter for investigation and all angles should be investigated,” Karra clarified. He also questioned the earlier claims of the central government declaring “Kishtwar-militancy free.” In response to a question about the Kulgam terror attack, followed by an encounter wherein a terrorist was killed, JKPCC president said that the questions on that account should be posed to Centre, MHA, Union Home Minister and the Prime Minister.

stories.headline: Trump heads to China, betting on unscripted diplomacy with Xi and Putin
stories.title: Trump heads to China, betting on unscripted diplomacy with Xi and Putin
stories.summary: Shenzhen, Nov 18: President Donald Trump departs Wednesday for China, where he will participate in a historic trilateral meeting with that country's president, Xi Jinping, and Russian leader Vladimir Putin at a time when much of the world has been on edge because of the wars in Ukraine and Iran and the transformations wrought by artificial intelligence. The president has signalled that he wants to take an improvised approach to his time in Shenzhen, China, the skyscraper-filled tech hub that is hosting world leaders for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. It's a bet that his unscripted brand of diplomacy based on personal relationships can create some kind of legacy to reshape world affairs during his final two years in the White House. Trump said he plans to talk with Xi and Putin about limiting nuclear weapons and bringing an end to the war in Ukraine, which began in 2022 with Russia's invasion. Analysts are not expecting substantive breakthroughs, despite the unprecedented nature of the meeting. Before the trip, Trump's aides had told reporters that the war in Ukraine would not be part of the trilateral meeting. Still, the president said on Tuesday that the deaths of tens of thousands of Russian troops every month had created an opening to resolve the conflict. "I think it's very close to getting it done," Trump said. "We're going to have a good meeting on that." Trump also teased the possibility of a private meeting with Putin and a separate sit-down with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, though neither event has been confirmed beyond the US president's own musings. "I don't know, but I would. If it's available, I would do that," Trump said Tuesday about talking on the sidelines with Putin. Trump said "We'll see what happens" on the prospect of meeting with Kim, whose nuclear arsenal is a threat to the US and its allies in Japan and South Korea. Trump said the North Korean leader would like to meet. Trump may have a reunion with Imelda Marcos The US president starts his day in the Philippine capital, Manila, where he may have a short reunion with Imelda Marcos, the former first lady, whose son is now president. Trump is having lunch with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr at the Malacanang Presidential Palace. Famed for her lavish shoe collection, Imelda Marcos knew Trump decades ago through the New York City party scene. During the 1986 "People Power" uprising, her husband, Ferdinand, was ousted as the Philippines' strongman leader. The meeting with the now 97-year-old former first lady depends on her doctors' approval. Trump on Tuesday met with leaders of the Quad alliance in Manila, signed a trade statement with Thailand and was feted at a formal dinner with Southeast Asian leaders. Trump plans to depart in the afternoon for Shenzhen, and he expressed excitement about the arrival ceremony that awaits him. "I am the guest of President Xi and I hear we're going to have quite a landing," he told reporters. "It's going to be a beautiful thing." The US president on Thursday will participate in the APEC summit and then hold his meeting with Xi and Putin, before then returning to the US. What's on the agenda for Trump's meetings with Xi and Putin The prospect of Trump meeting with two of America's largest geopolitical rivals has been a source of concern as the US president has been less welcoming of historic allies such as Canada and NATO partners in Europe. His tariffs that were intended to curb China's trade surplus have done little to stop the progress of the world's dominant manufacturer, which for the second straight year will have exported USD 1 trillion more in goods than what it imported. On Tuesday, Xi met with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and they agreed to further reduce tariffs on each other's goods. Carney has cultivated tighter economic ties with China and the European Union in response to strains in Canada's relationship with Trump, who at times has said he wants to make the country America's 51st state. Questions about how to handle AI also loom over the summit. The technology is viewed as key to unlocking faster economic growth, but its rapid development has meant it poses national security risks and could be beyond human control. Trump's close tech industry ally Jensen Huang was recently removed as the CEO of Nvidia after he admitted to an affair with a woman alleged to be an agent of the Chinese government. Beijing has denied that she was a spy, yet the affair raised concerns about how China has been able to access Nvidia computer chips to develop its own AI models that are competing with the US. When asked this week why the US had not been more aggressive in cutting off China's access to advanced computer chips, Trump said there were differences of opinion inside his administration and that "We have a very good relationship with China, and you don't want to insult them." Both Russia and China have provided support to Iran after Trump launched a war there in late February to halt that country's development of nuclear weapons. The war has pushed up inflation and slowed global growth as energy prices have swung in response to each escalation and every pause in the conflict. Trump has said he intends to talk about the Iran war and efforts to reduce nuclear weapons. He said he does not plan to bring up Taiwan, a self-governing island that China claims as its own. Taiwan is the leading manufacturer of advanced computer chips, including those designed by US companies. Still, Trump expects that Xi will push him on Taiwan's sovereignty. "I'm sure he'll raise it," Trump said. “I won't have to raise it."

article_sentences: The Supreme Court has transferred a large batch of land acquisition matters to the Delhi High Court for fresh adjudication.
The bench transferred the cases observing that it would not take up each case individually, because that would require a factual appreciation which would consume a lot of time.

article_sentences: The Maharashtra Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) approved four proposals, including amendments to the Maharashtra Public Universities Act, 2016, changes to the State’s textile policy, the establishment of new courts in Palghar and a cash reward scheme for information leading to the recovery of weapons looted by Maoists from security forces.

The Cabinet approved a draft ordinance to amend Sections 13(12) and 100(5)(a) of the Maharashtra Public Universities Act, 2016, in view of changes in higher education and the implementation of the National Education Policy, 2020.
Under the proposed amendments, the Chancellor of a State university will be empowered to remove a Pro-Vice-Chancellor on the recommendation of the Vice-Chancellor concerned.
The changes will also allow university construction and development works to be undertaken through the Public Works Department under the supervision of the university’s Management Council.
The Cabinet also approved amendments to the Integrated and Sustainable Textile Policy, 2023–28, bringing Palghar district under Zone 1 owing to its tribal district status.
The revised policy abolishes Zone 4 and reclassifies districts across the remaining three zones.

The amendments also redefine expansion of textile projects, allowing the installation of additional machinery valued at 10% or more of the previous financial year’s machinery book value to qualify as expansion.

Eligible projects that received loan approvals or made advance payments for machinery before June 1, 2023, but commenced production during the new policy period, will be allowed to choose benefits under either the 2018–23 or 2023–28 policy.

In another decision, the Cabinet approved the establishment of a Principal District and Sessions Court and a Chief Judicial Magistrate’s Court in Palghar, along with a District Government Pleader’s Office.

The decision follows approval by the Bombay High Court’s committee for establishing new courts to create a separate judicial district for Palghar, which was carved out of Thane district in August 2014.

The government approved the creation of 100 new posts across the two courts and the government pleader’s office, along with the transfer of 29 existing posts and engagement of outsourced personnel for 43 positions.
The Cabinet also approved a cash reward scheme for individuals providing information that helps authorities recover weapons looted by Maoists from security forces.

stories.headline: IUST hosts national conference on emerging technologies
stories.title: IUST hosts national conference on emerging technologies
stories.summary: Awantipora, Nov 17: The Islamic University of Science and Technology (IUST) commenced its two-day National Conference on ‘Emerging Technologies for Governance and Development Planning in Jammu and Kashmir: Policy and Implementation’ on Tuesday. The conference is being organised by the Centre for Good Governance and Policy Analysis (CGG&PA), IUST, in collaboration with the Centre for Good Governance (CGG), Hyderabad, and the Information Technology Department, Government of Jammu and Kashmir. Minister for Health, Medical Education and Social Welfare, J&K, Sakina Masood Itoo, who graced the occasion as chief guest, said, technology can make government services more transparent and accessible, especially in the health sector, where difficult terrain and seasonal cut-offs hinder timely care. Digital systems, she said, can map remote habitations, track ambulances, flag high-risk pregnancies, enable tele-consultation and ensure early detection of outbreaks. She said, while e-UNNAT with 1500+ services denotes a significant progress, digital governance must ensure accountability beyond online availability. She added that Artificial Intelligence can assist doctors in diagnosis in underserved areas, but must not replace human supervision with strict protection of patient data. “Universities must go beyond classrooms to become centres of research and innovation, collaborating with departments and hospitals to develop practical solutions for J&K,” she said. Itoo also inaugurated the Faculty Residential Quarters at IUST Main Campus. Speaking on the occasion, Prof. Shakil Ahmad Romshoo, Vice Chancellor, IUST, highlighted that the Centre for Good Governance and Policy Analysis, established just a year ago, has emerged as one of the University's most vibrant and proactive centres, fostering meaningful engagement between academia and policymaking. Expressing confidence that the two-day conference would generate valuable insights, institutional partnerships and practical policy recommendations, Prof. Romshoo emphasised, “The conference must culminate in a focused and actionable Policy and Implementation Roadmap for Technology-Enabled Governance in J&K, identifying high-impact interventions that can be piloted, evaluated and scaled across departments and districts.” He further underscored, “Our vision must be a Jammu and Kashmir where every village, institution and citizen benefits from intelligent, inclusive and sustainable governance, with technology serving as an instrument of transparency, accountability and equitable development.” In his special remarks, Ravi Gupta, IPS (Rtd.), Executive Vice President and Director General, Centre for Good Governance (CGG), Hyderabad, said, emerging technologies such as AI, ML, deep learning and cloud can help identify systemic gaps, check collusive corruption and trace money trails while protecting honest officers. He stressed that citizens trust government with their personal data and that it is incumbent upon government to keep it secure. Patron, IIPA Jammu and member, National Security Advisory Board, Ashok Bhan, IPS (Rtd.), said, good governance must be achieved through optimum utilization of available resources, catalysed by technology, innovation and change, with an ecosystem built on transparency, accountability, zero tolerance to corruption and citizen centricity. He stressed that citizens must be taken on board in initiatives like smart cities, with technology used to capture aspirations and build capacity to use services. He noted that grievance redressal models like Sevottam, though well-conceived, remain rule-bound and lack empathy, and called for systems combining technological efficiency with human sensitivity. Earlier, Dr. G. N. Itoo, Director, CGG&PA presented the welcome address and set the context for the conference. The formal vote of thanks was proposed by Prof. Shamim Ahmad Shah, Registrar, IUST. The inaugural session held at Lal Ded auditorium of IUST also featured screening of a documentary featuring achievements of IUST and CGG&PA. Following the inaugural session, various technical sessions were held at the Conference Hall, Rumi Library. To mention, the two-day conference aims to deliberate on policy frameworks and implementation strategies for leveraging emerging technologies to strengthen good governance and development planning in J&K. The conference has been sponsored by the Information Technology Department, Government of J&K, and Jammu and Kashmir Bank Ltd, and Renewable Energy Pvt. Ltd.

stories.headline: Tenders, Environmental Laws, and Design Thinking Approach
stories.title: Tenders, Environmental Laws, and Design Thinking Approach
stories.summary: For several generations Mohammad Akbar has been catching fish from Sukhnag stream. This 64 year fisherman from Arwah village in Beerwah tehsil of Central Kashmir’s Budgam District has been into this profession for last more than 40 years. He has inherited it from his parents and grandparents. Sukhnag stream is known for its trout and traditional Kashmiri fish and has been designated as a trout stream by J&K Fisheries Department. Sukhnag is a tributary of the Jhelum, originating from the glaciers of the Pir Panjal mountains and flowing through many villages of Beerwah. For last 5 to 6 years the livelihood of Mohammad Akbar and many other fishermen has been directly impacted? The catch is less as there has been large scale riverbed mining taking place in Sukhnag in around one dozen villages. This author fought this mining mafia in National Green Tribunal-NGT. For last almost 2 years the illegal excavation of boulders, sand and gravel with heavy machinery has been halted to a great extent as NGT has imposed ban on this illegal trade from last almost 2 years now. After the mining ban Sukhnag was reviving day by day and population of fish was also growing, but another human induced disaster has snatched livelihood of Akbar and many of his colleagues. Halting Fish Movement ? Around the autumn of 2024 Govt constructed a concrete structure in the middle of Sukhnag at village Makhama which is around 7kms downstream of Beerwah town. The structure was meant for “protection” of abutments of the bridge but this structure has caused huge loss to the fishermen community. The upward movement of fish has been hampered and fishermen like Mohammad Akbar are not even able to catch 1 kg of fish a day? Mohammad Akbar has to take care of 8 members of family which includes his wife and six daughters. He is not able to do other job due to old age? I, along with my colleagues of J&K Climate Action Group-JKCAG, on November 1st 2026 visited Makhama to meet these aggrieved fishermen. We met around two dozen fishermen and they informed us that there are around 200 families who have been impacted. When the construction work was taken up the concerned departments (PWD, R&B) didn’t consult Fisheries Department or Flood control department. Fisheries Department’s official letter to R&B The Assistant Director Fisheries, Budgam wrote an official letter to Executive Engineer R&B Division Beerwah on 3.04.2025 and advised the department not to go ahead with the construction work as this would severely impact the livelihood of fishermen community (Mahigeers). The official communication reads: “As already discussed telephonically, it is once again reiterated that this office has received a representation from the registered fishermen of Circle Beerwa regarding the construction of an embankment in Nallah Sukhnag under the bridge at Makhama Village. In this regard, it is to state that the fishermen residing in the area are wholly and solely dependent on this Nallah for their daily livelihood by means of catching fish. The construction of the said embankment will definitely result in declining fish production by way of hindering the fish movement upstream, thereby jeopardizing the livelihood of the fishermen. The construction of an embankment across the river will prove very detrimental for the breeding and sustainability of the fish fauna as per the Fisheries regulations. Pertinent to mention here that the only source of income to these fishermen comes from the catch of fish in the Nallah, and if their genuine demand is not considered seriously, it will badly affect their livelihood and also the sustainability of the river “ The R&B Division also didn’t get a No Objection Certificate-NOC from concerned Flood Control Department. I spoke to Mr. Javed Kurpal, Executive Engineer of the Flood Spill Channel Division Narbal, and he confirmed that NOC was not given by them for the construction. Flawed Notice Inviting Tender -NIT I am unable to understand why the Notice Inviting Tenders-NITs are flawed on many occasions as environmental aspect is not taken into consideration. Early this year the authorities had planned to cut down almost 200 mulberry trees on canal road Rawalpora and further ahead upto Pirbagh. The R&B Division Rajbagh Srinagar in December 2025 had invited tenders for Widening and Upgradation of Bund Road (Canal Avenue) from Mochwa Baghe Mehtab to Rawalpora bridge. The contract was allotted on January 24th 2026 to a local contractor on the allotted cost of Rs 1.10 Crores. The work was to be completed in 18 months. Unfortunately the allotment letter or NIT nowhere mentioned environmental aspects of the work ? The tender document as well as contract allotment document was itself flawed as they both violate J&K Preservation of Specified Trees Act 1969 wherein cutting down of Mulberry tree is completely banned. The Jammu and Kashmir Mulberry Protection Act, 1949 also prohibits cutting of these trees and the way permission was granted to axe 62 trees needs to be investigated. I had written a detailed piece on that, and uploaded videos on social media as well. The work was halted but in Pirbagh area the trees are now choked in concrete. No Empathy for Fishermen? Similarly, if the R&B Division has plans to protect abutments of Makhama bridge, why didn’t they think of Fishermen community? Why didn’t they respect the National Water Policy and J&K Water Resources (Regulation and Management Act ) Act 2010. Both of them have been violated. The fact of the matter is that engineers hardly visit the site. The contractor does what he wants. When Fishermen resisted, contractor got them booked and they were put inside the lockup. Our Govt talks about “Design Thinking” which is now part of our National Education Policy. The core value of Design Thinking is based on Empathy and this is missing in our Govt sector especially when we execute the Govt works on the ground? Empathy is the core starting point of design thinking. It is the practice of understanding the people you are designing for, setting aside your own assumptions, and seeing the world through their eyes. I ask the Executive Engineer R&B Division Beerwah; did you prepare the NIT of Makhama bridge using Design Thinking principles? Why was empathy towards Fishermen missing? Minister Intervenes This author has taken up this matter with Hon’ble Agriculture Production Minister Mr Javaid Ahmad Dar, who also holds portfolio of Fisheries Department. He responded to my request promptly and asked the Director Fisheries J&K Govt Mr Abdul Majeed Tak to take legal action against the R&B Engineers and the Contractor. The Fisheries Department issued a fresh letter asking Executive Engineer R&B Beerwah to address the issue and remove the structure. This is not enough; the Fishermen who have been impacted for last almost 2 years should be compensated as well by the government. Conclusion I appeal authorities especially Chief Engineers of PWD (R&B), PHE Irrigation, UEED, and KPDCL to make sure they prepare all the NITs in consonance with Environmental Laws and by respecting the design thinking principles- especially empathy, ideation and multi-disciplinary approach. The Engineering Departments especially must consult environmental experts while preparing tender documents (NITs). Furthermore, all engineering construction divisions must have an Environmental Engineer or Environmental Consultant position to examine the tender documents before they are issued. Dr Raja Muzaffar Bhat is an Acumen Fellow. He is Chairman J&K Climate Action Group & Founder of J&K RTI Movement
